nodes.question: What are the four main politically relevant worldviews identified by Cultural Theory?
nodes.answer: The four main politically relevant worldviews identified by Cultural Theory are egalitarianism, individualism, hierarchy, and fatalism.
nodes.paragraph: Political cultures point to the importance of mean- ing (Mamadouh, 1999b, p. 477). Cultural Theory (CT) is a long-established approach for such analyses (Thompson et al., 1990). CT, originating from the works of Douglas (1978) and Douglas and Wildavsky (1982) and developed by Thompson et al. (1990), analyzes how actors perceive the world (related risks, problems, solutions, etc.) and interact with their surroundings based on their values and beliefs (Chuang et al., 2020; Tansey, 2004). We set out to explore how CT could assist in understanding the roots of different perceptions in EU forest policy, investigating two main research questions: 1. How do EU forest policy actors envisage forests and their ecosystem services in terms of perceived problems, preferred solutions, and responsibilities to govern forests? Policy Sciences 2. How can Cultural Theory contribute to understanding overlaps and differences in these views and which theoretical implications could a better understanding of these over - laps and differences offer? Theoretical framework: cultural theory Cultural Theory identifies four main politically relevant worldviews: egalitarianism, indi- vidualism, hierarchy, and fatalism.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What belief did people in late Middle Ages Denmark hold about pregnant women and bees?
nodes.answer: It was believed that a woman could not get pregnant if she ate bees.
nodes.paragraph: Propolis, a sticky, resinous substance, has long been used for medici - nal purposes and was mentioned in Nordic drug tariffs and pharmacopeias as early as the seventeenth and eight - eenth centuries. However, it was mainly used externally, especially as a cerata. Both yellow and white wax are found in older European pharmacopeias and were used as protective and covering agents and were included as ingredients in cerata, ointments, and plasters [17]. Yellow wax was prescribed into the nineteenth century as a pal - liative for intestinal disorders. Even the bees themselves could be prescribed in folk medicine. During the late Middle Ages in Denmark, it was believed that a woman could not get pregnant if she ate bees. Rubbing a crushed bee against your teeth prevented toothache, according to a record from Denmark [14]. The period of beekeeping commercialization Ukrainian beekeeper Petro Ivanovich Prokopovych (1775 1850) is considered one of the founders of com - mercial beekeeping and the father of the modern hive because he invented the frame hive in 1814.
